items.title: How to win any jelly bean guessing jar
items.summary: How to win any jelly bean guessing jar. Mark Rober's method: count the beans touching a line straight across the jar, count the same line on the side, then count straight up, and multiply. His jar came out to 10 x 10 x 16 = 1,600. The real count was 1,621, so he was off by 21. Then he ate the extra 21 so his number was perfect. Idea and method: Mark Rober. Clips: Mark Rober, "Jelly Bean Guessing Game HACK" (YouTube Short); Pixabay footage and photos by Tariq786, anncapictures, aframeinmotion, Sophieja23, pixel1, stevepb, FoodieFactor, artsysolomon, Kathas_Fotos, ClickerHappy, Ogutier, eulainemc, igorovsyannykov. #Shorts #math #jellybeans #lifehacks If you've got a friend who loses every office raffle, send them this. And tell them to skip lunch.

items.title: Why pools smell like chlorine
items.summary: Why pools smell like chlorine. Mark Rober filled two buckets with clean water and four times the normal amount of chlorine, then added a tiny splash of pee to bucket B. A day later, bucket A smelled like water and bucket B smelled exactly like a pool. The CDC says that "chlorine" smell is probably chloramines, which form when chlorine combines with pee and sweat. Idea and experiment: Mark Rober. Source: CDC, Preventing Eye Irritation from Pool Chemicals (cdc.gov). Clips: Mark Rober, "How much pee is in a pool?" (YouTube Short); Pixabay footage by xat-ch, BernardMedia-DR, Vladvictoria, jcax2, olenailinska, Ian5152, stefaniejockschat, Coverr-Free-Footage, flutie8211, swistakens, MilanWulf. Send this to the friend who swears they've never peed in a pool. #Shorts #science #swimming #pool

items.title: Why your voice sounds weird on recordings
items.summary: Why your voice sounds weird on recordings. When you talk, sound reaches your ear through the air and through your skull. Bone carries frequencies up to about 1 kHz, so you sound deeper to yourself. A microphone only hears the air path. Source: JAIST (Unoki), Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, 2021. Idea: ASAP SCIENCE. Clips: Daniel Thrasher, "When you hear your own voice for the first time" (YouTube); Pixabay footage by Engin_Akyurt, stevediaz, MrWashingt0n, intersubjektiv, magicmore, NeuroPixels, VFS_World, Bastien86, flutie8211, iwsky, conte_public, mephala1980. Do you hate your recorded voice? So send this to the friend who refuses to listen to their own voice notes. #Shorts #voice #science #sound

items.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
items.summary: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk...
